after.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}(x+y)\,dx+x\,dy,$ where $C$ is a portion of the parabola parametrized by $r(t)=2t\,i+(2-{t}^{2})\,j$ for $t\in [0,1].$
after.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=2t,\,y(t)=2-{t}^{2}.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2-{t}^{2})\,j \\  & =2\,i-2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}(x+y)\,dx+x\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(x+y)\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[(x+y)\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}]dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(2t+2-{t}^{2})\cdot 2+2t\cdot (-2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}-6{t}^{2}+4t+4\,\text{d}t \\  & ={[-2{t}^{3}+2{t}^{2}+4t]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(-2+2+4)-0 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}x\,dx-z\,dy+y\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the curve $r(t)=3{t}^{2}\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,k$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ].$
after.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=3{t}^{2},\,y(t)=3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,z(t)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,k \\  & =6t\,i+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$

Question 3
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫C−ydx+xdy+z2dz, where C is a portion of the curve r(t)=2cos⁡ti−2sin⁡tj+t2k for t∈[0,3π2]?

a
∫03π/22t3+2dt
b
∫03π/22t3+sin2⁡tdt
c
∫03π/22t5−4dt
d
∫03π/22t4−2sin2⁡tdt
e
∫03π/22t4−2cos⁡tdt
Submit

decision.explanation: Here x=2cos(t), y=−2sin(t), z=t², so x′=−2sin(t), y′=−2cos(t), and z′=2t. Thus −yx′+xy′+z²z′=−4sin²(t)−4cos²(t)+2t⁵=2t⁵−4. Keeping the limits 0 to 3π/2 gives option c.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}-y\,dx+x\,dy+{z}^{2}\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the curve $r(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+{t}^{2}\,k$ for $t\in [0,\frac{3\pi }{2}]?$
after.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(t)=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,z(t)={t}^{2}.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,k \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}-y\,dx+x\,dy+{z}^{2}\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /2}-y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+{z}^{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /2}(-y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+{z}^{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /2}2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)+{t}^{4}\cdot (2t)\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /2}2{t}^{5}-4{sin}^{2}⁡t-4{cos}^{2}⁡t\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /2}2{t}^{5}-4\,dt\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫C−ydx+xdy+z2dz, where C is a portion of the curve r(t)=2cos⁡ti−2sin⁡tj+t2k for t∈[0,3π2]?

a
∫03π/22t3+2dt
b
∫03π/22t3+sin2⁡tdt
c

EXPLANATION

Along the curve, we have x(t)=2cos⁡t,y(t)=−2sin⁡t,z(t)=t2.

The derivative of r(t) is given by

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj+dzdtk=ddt(2cos⁡t)i+ddt(−2sin⁡t)j+ddt(t2)k=−2sin⁡ti−2cos⁡tj+2tk.

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

∫C−ydx+xdy+z2dz=∫03π/2−ydxdtdt+xdydtdt+z2dzdtdt=∫03π/2(−ydxdt+xdydt+z2dzdt)dt=∫03π/22sin⁡t⋅(−2sin⁡t)+2cos⁡t⋅(−2cos⁡t)+t4⋅(2t)dt=∫03π/22t5−4sin2⁡t−4cos2⁡tdt=∫03π/22t5−4dt

content.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(t)=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,z(t)={t}^{2}.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,k \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}-y\,dx+x\,dy+{z}^{2}\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /2}-y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+{z}^{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /2}(-y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+{z}^{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /2}2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)+{t}^{4}\cdot (2t)\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /2}2{t}^{5}-4{sin}^{2}⁡t-4{cos}^{2}⁡t\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /2}2{t}^{5}-4\,dt\end{aligned}
$$

Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Along the curve, we have x(t)=t,y(t)=t2,z(t)=t3.

The derivative of r(t) is given by

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj+dzdtk=ddt(t)i+ddt(t2)j+ddt(t3)k=i+2tj+3t2j.

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

content.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=t,\,y(t)={t}^{2},\,z(t)={t}^{3}.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\,k \\  & =\,i+2t\,j+3{t}^{2}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}xy\,dx+y\,dy+z\,dz & ={\int }_{3}^{5}xy\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{5}(xy\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{5}{t}^{3}\cdot (1)+{t}^{2}\cdot (2t)+{t}^{3}\cdot (3{t}^{2})\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{5}3{t}^{5}+3{t}^{3}\,dt \\  & =3{\int }_{3}^{5}{t}^{5}+{t}^{3}\,dt\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫Cln⁡xdx−zdy+y2dz, where C is a portion of the curve r(t)=ti+t2j+t2k for t∈[2,6]?

a
∫265ln⁡t+4t4dt
b
∫26ln⁡t+2t5−2t3dt
c
∫265t5−3t3dt
d
∫26ln⁡t+5tdt
e
∫26ln2⁡t−2t3dt
Submit

decision.explanation: With x=t, y=t², z=t², we have dx=dt and dy=dz=2t dt. Thus ln(x) dx−z dy+y² dz=[ln(t)−2t³+2t⁵]dt. Keeping the limits [2,6] gives option b.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,dx-z\,dy+{y}^{2}\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the curve $r(t)=t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+{t}^{2}\,k$ for $t\in [2,6]?$
after.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=t,\,y(t)={t}^{2},\,z(t)={t}^{2}.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,k \\  & =\,i+2t\,j+2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,dx-z\,dy+{y}^{2}\,dz & ={\int }_{2}^{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt-z\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{6}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}-z\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡t\cdot (1)-{t}^{2}\cdot (2t)+{t}^{4}\cdot (2t)\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡t+2{t}^{5}-2{t}^{3}\,dt\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫Cln⁡xdx−zdy+y2dz, where C is a portion of the curve r(t)=ti+t2j+t2k for t∈[2,6]?

a
∫265ln⁡t+4t4dt
b
∫26ln⁡t+2t5−2t3dt
c
∫265t5−3t3dt
d
∫26ln⁡t+5tdt
e
∫26ln2⁡t−2t3dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Along the curve, we have x(t)=t,y(t)=t2,z(t)=t2.

The derivative of r(t) is given by

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj+dzdtk=ddt(t)i+ddt(t2)j+ddt(t2)k=i+2tj+2tk.

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

∫Cln⁡xdx−zdy+y2dz=∫26ln⁡xdxdtdt−zdydtdt+y2dzdtdt=∫26(ln⁡xdxdt−zdydt+y2dzdt)dt=∫26ln⁡t⋅(1)−t2⋅(2t)+t4⋅(2t)dt=∫26ln⁡t+2t5−2t3dt

content.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,dx-z\,dy+{y}^{2}\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the curve $r(t)=t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+{t}^{2}\,k$ for $t\in [2,6]?$
content.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=t,\,y(t)={t}^{2},\,z(t)={t}^{2}.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,k \\  & =\,i+2t\,j+2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,dx-z\,dy+{y}^{2}\,dz & ={\int }_{2}^{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt-z\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{6}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}-z\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡t\cdot (1)-{t}^{2}\cdot (2t)+{t}^{4}\cdot (2t)\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡t+2{t}^{5}-2{t}^{3}\,dt\end{aligned}
$$
